<p class="source-citation"><a href="https://docs.ogc.org/is/18-062r2/18-062r2.html#toc21">Published source: OGC 18-062r2, 1.0.0 (toc21)</a>. Modified Building Blocks rendition of OGC 18-062r2 (2021). This Intellectual Property includes modifications that have not been approved or adopted by the Open Geospatial Consortium (LICENSOR). The published source is an Approved OGC Standard; this reconstructed rendition is not an OGC-approved publication. In case of any discrepancy the published HTML prevails.</p>

<div id="_requirements_class_core">
<span id="toc21"></span>
<p id="_1938aabe-a587-dac8-ca50-87e03d60ac05">The following section describes the core requirements class.</p>
<div id="_overview"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc22">7.1.  Overview</h2><span id="rc_core"></span><!-- requirements-class -->
<p id="_d5078b41-60b4-9400-b586-698a11c45153">A server that implements the OGC API — Processes Standard provides access to processes.</p>
<p id="_4a2f1ac1-089a-13d9-0cb0-3233704db3f2">Each implementation of the OGC API — Processes Standard has a single <tt>LandingPage</tt> (path <tt>/</tt>) that provides links to</p>
<ul id="_4c912bf4-3c5f-2bed-10d5-ff9f42f81081">
<li>
<p id="_dca52042-85ee-7419-1808-2e92df31b5a7">The <tt>APIDefinition</tt> (no fixed path),</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_b9369257-fe05-d2ff-67b3-001aababae7c">The <tt>Conformance</tt> statements (path <tt>/conformance</tt>),</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_dfa3efd8-9a96-8274-28b9-ae5bab2f6f80">The <tt>processes</tt> metadata (path <tt>/processes</tt>).</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="_020c5fd3-734e-130f-9b4d-29e1d296f3d5">Note that additional requirements classes may introduce additional links for the landing page.</p>
<p id="_7c2d97fc-c26f-3ccd-f0ed-964bd08ee54c">The <tt>APIDefinition</tt> describes the capabilities of the server that can be used by
clients to connect to the server or by development tools to support the
implementation of servers and clients. Accessing the <tt>APIDefinition</tt> using
HTTP GET returns a description of the API.</p>
<p id="_a9c00169-510f-c8a0-57d7-e6450c1137fa">Accessing <tt>Conformance</tt> using HTTP GET returns a list of URIs of
requirements classes implemented by the server.</p>
<p id="_39cc6e18-7f26-8826-ef11-452523e719c0">The list of processes contains a summary of each process offered by the OGC API — Processes implementation, including the link to a more detailed description of the process.</p>
<p id="_6cb24ac1-c7c3-459a-befd-16e8e48de3f8">The <a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a> contains information about inputs and outputs and a link to the execution-endpoint for the process.</p>
<p id="_238c4fca-9e40-efe7-e8bd-2fb4b8dd6a7f">A HTTP POST request to the execution-endpoint creates a new job. The inputs and outputs need to be passed in a JSON execute-request.</p>
<p id="_4d54fd62-fd07-e214-55db-d75460681536">The URL for accessing status information is delivered in the HTTP header <tt>location</tt>.</p>
<p id="_a6b605c0-5bc2-f8eb-da06-2fc78444d39c">After a process is finished (status = success/failed), the results/exceptions can be retrieved.</p>
<div class="figure" id="img_core">
<img height="745" src="data:image/png;base64," width="700"/>
<p class="FigureTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 1 — Resources in the Core requirements class</p></div>

<div id="sc_landing_page"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc23">7.2.  Retrieve the API landing page</h2><p id="_8fc4df06-07b4-a1c6-b2ce-f7235cd4cde4">The following section defines the requirements to retrieve an API landing page.</p>
<div id="_operation"><h3 class="published-heading">7.2.1.  Operation</h3>
<span id="req_core_landingpage-op"></span><!-- requirement: core/landingpage-op -->
</div>
<div id="_response"><h3 class="published-heading">7.2.2.  Response</h3><span id="req_core_landingpage-success"></span><!-- requirement: core/landingpage-success -->
<div class="Note" id="_6ccc2aa9-cc51-9b98-8453-23187b776131"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  1</span>  The term “<i>…​based upon the OpenAPI 3.0 schema…​</i>” used in the requirements of this specification means that OpenAPI 3.0 is used to define:</p><ul id="_a4586c4f-01ff-42ea-6fc4-4f3234457e8c">
<li>
<p id="_d8e4b290-3287-bdee-f706-106fd6e1caae">all the required properties of the respective request/response schema,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_847e1fbb-5610-651c-e1ea-45acf817170b">and any optional properties of the respective request/response schema.</p>
</li>
</ul><p id="_b6efe38f-2d7b-7b07-9052-6d4be1e0b5da">It also means that unless explicitly excluded these schemas are extensible with additional properties not defined in the schema using the <a href="https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/main/versions/3.0.0.md#schemaObject"><tt>additionalProperties</tt></a> mechanism defined in the <a href="https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/main/versions/3.0.0.md">OpenAPI 3.0 specification</a>.</p></div>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_de048380-b57d-574c-a135-3cefe1904efc">type: object<br/>required:<br/>  - links<br/>properties:<br/>  title:<br/>    type: string<br/>    example: Example processing server<br/>  description:<br/>    type: string<br/>    example: Example server implementing the OGC API - Processes 1.0 Standard<br/>  links:<br/>    type: array<br/>    items:<br/>      $ref: "link.yaml"</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 2 — Schema for the landing page</p>
<div class="Note" id="_7722b32c-4132-0ce4-fc1a-357daf9bc1c1"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  2</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/landingPage.yaml"><tt>landingPage.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="link-schema">type: object<br/>required:<br/>  - href<br/>properties:<br/>  href:<br/>    type: string<br/>  rel:<br/>    type: string<br/>    example: service<br/>  type:<br/>    type: string<br/>    example: application/json<br/>  hreflang:<br/>    type: string<br/>    example: en<br/>  title:<br/>    type: string</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 3 — Schema for a link</p>
<div class="Note" id="_9d0e85fd-d4ec-cc7d-1d6a-4fca0a58fae7"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  3</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/link.yaml"><tt>link.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Example  — Landing page response document</p><div class="example" id="_8a320c19-bf7e-768e-8950-6ca33eafcc4d"><pre class="prettyprint" id="_8389c116-bb59-0cc5-32a2-cc250e43ea85">{<br/>	"links": [{<br/>		"href": "http://processing.example.org/oapi-p?f=application/json",<br/>		"rel": "self",<br/>		"type": "application/json",<br/>		"title": "This document"<br/>	},{<br/>		"href": "http://processing.example.org/oapi-p?f=text/html",<br/>		"rel": "alternate",<br/>		"type": "text/html",<br/>		"title": "This document as HTML"<br/>	},<br/>	{<br/>		"href": "http://processing.example.org/oapi-p/api?f=application/json",<br/>		"rel": "service-desc",<br/>		"type": "application/json",<br/>		"title": "API definition for this endpoint as JSON"<br/>	},<br/>	{<br/>		"href": "http://processing.example.org/oapi-p/api?f=text/html",<br/>		"rel": "service-desc",<br/>		"type": "text/html",<br/>		"title": "API definition for this endpoint as HTML"<br/>	},<br/>	{<br/>		"href": "http://processing.example.org/oapi-p/conformance",<br/>		"rel": "http://www.opengis.net/def/rel/ogc/1.0/conformance",<br/>		"type": "application/json",<br/>		"title": "OGC API - Processes conformance classes implemented by this server"<br/>	},<br/>	{<br/>		"href": "http://processing.example.org/oapi-p/processes",<br/>		"rel": "http://www.opengis.net/def/rel/ogc/1.0/processes",<br/>		"type": "application/json",<br/>		"title": "Metadata about the processes"<br/>	},<br/>	{<br/>		"href": "http://processing.example.org/oapi-p/jobs",<br/>		"rel": "http://www.opengis.net/def/rel/ogc/1.0/job-list",<br/>		"title": "The endpoint for job monitoring"<br/>	}]<br/>}</pre>
</div></div>

<div id="sc_api_definition"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc24">7.3.  Retrieve an API definition</h2><p id="_96b32b54-6158-282e-8553-0fd4a7f3ef14">The following section defines the requirements to retrieve an API definition.</p>
<div id="_operation_2"><h3 class="published-heading">7.3.1.  Operation</h3><p id="_7aeb1b64-317b-0503-4959-ea028999a108">Every implementation of OGC API — Processes provides an API definition that describes the capabilities
of the server. This definition is used by developers to understand the API,
by software clients to connect to the server, or
by development tools to support the implementation of servers and clients.</p>
<span id="req_core_api-definition-op"></span><!-- requirement: core/api-definition-op -->
<span id="per_core_api-definition-uri"></span><!-- permission: core/api-definition-uri -->
<p id="_c55716d1-90c6-909e-4e09-442466b1472f">Note that multiple API definition formats can be supported.</p></div>
<div id="_response_2"><h3 class="published-heading">7.3.2.  Response</h3><span id="req_core_api-definition-success"></span><!-- requirement: core/api-definition-success -->
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_api_definition-oas" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 2</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/api-definition-oas</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p id="_ed8890b6-4885-c624-0cdf-114f53d38109">If the API definition document uses the OpenAPI Specification 3.0,
the document SHOULD conform to the
<a href="#rc_oas30">OpenAPI Specification 3.0 requirements class</a>.</p></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p id="_52917864-2c1b-fba9-70f6-4ceb7c77bf6f">If multiple API definition formats are supported by a server, use
content negotiation to select the desired representation.<div class="Note" id="_8e34b897-8d3f-fd93-9f56-a955a8e68f49"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE</span>  Two common approaches are:</p><ul id="_82c1aa69-8ea7-c59b-9df5-3cf09c8a2768">
<li>
<p id="_a796a6b7-48da-b9d0-94d3-330090e975da">an additional path for each encoding of each resource (this can be expressed,
for example, using format specific suffixes like “.html”);</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_d62edf1a-6c63-804e-f3d4-8dbf6ee1a1c3">an additional query parameter (for example, “accept” or “f”) that overrides
the Accept header of the HTTP request.</p>
</li>
</ul></div></p>
<p id="_da8485db-503a-7684-bbbe-6c0ab2b81944">The API definition document describes the API. In other words,
there is no need to include the <tt>/api</tt> operation in the API definition itself.</p>
<p id="_960503a0-db50-5b8f-a73f-51208ada0531">The idea is that any implementation of OGC API — Processes can be used by developers that are familiar with
the API definition language(s) supported by the server. For example, if
an OpenAPI definition is used, it should be possible to create a working
client using the OpenAPI definition. The developer may need to learn a little
bit about geospatial data types, etc., but it should not be required to read
this standard to access the processes and results via the API.</p></div>
<div id="_error_situations_2"><h3 class="published-heading">7.3.3.  Error situations</h3>
<p id="_764634ca-c2c6-1631-f394-d0676456f59c">See <a href="#http_status_codes">Clause 7.5.1</a> for general guidance.</p>
</div></div>
<div id="sc_conformance_classes"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc25">7.4.  Declaration of conformance classes</h2><div id="_operation_3"><h3 class="published-heading">7.4.1.  Operation</h3><p id="_3368ce30-9f58-192c-9dd6-190f52954516">To support “generic” clients for accessing servers implementing OGC API — Processes in general — and
not “just” a specific API / server, the server has to declare the
requirements classes it implements and conforms to.</p>
<span id="req_core_conformance-op"></span><!-- requirement: core/conformance-op --></div>
<div id="_response_3"><h3 class="published-heading">7.4.2.  Response</h3><span id="req_core_conformance-success"></span><!-- requirement: core/conformance-success -->
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_c434040e-d6a0-a2fe-1165-3c55dccf55fa">type: object<br/>required:<br/>  - conformsTo<br/>properties:<br/>  conformsTo:<br/>    type: array<br/>    items:<br/>      type: string<br/>      example: "http://www.opengis.net/spec/ogcapi-processes-1/1.0/conf/core"</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 4 — Schema for the list of conformance classes</p>
<div class="Note" id="_94cbc898-a97f-4a68-2111-e96e4e4ebe0f"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/confClasses.yaml"><tt>confClasses.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Example  — Requirements class response document</p><div class="example" id="_bedc6c32-8a5b-94f8-53ee-301b8bf4877c"><p id="_1b4f903e-42ed-1935-0dd7-c0a6eb8eaa8f">This example response in JSON is for a server that supports OpenAPI 3.0 for
the API definition and HTML and JSON as encodings.</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_9e928171-6d55-192d-9571-b8a9686a31bf">{<br/>	"conformsTo": [<br/>		"http://www.opengis.net/spec/ogcapi-processes-1/1.0/conf/core",<br/>		"http://www.opengis.net/spec/ogcapi-processes-1/1.0/conf/json",<br/>		"http://www.opengis.net/spec/ogcapi-processes-1/1.0/conf/html",<br/>		"http://www.opengis.net/spec/ogcapi-processes-1/1.0/conf/oas30"<br/>	]<br/>}</pre>
</div></div>
<div id="_error_situations_3"><h3 class="published-heading">7.4.3.  Error situations</h3>
<p id="_b865deec-3bba-f844-ed5c-2ad88aa68080">See <a href="#http_status_codes">Clause 7.5.1</a> for general guidance.</p>
</div></div>
<div id="_use_of_http_1_1"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc26">7.5.  Use of HTTP 1.1</h2><span id="req_core_http"></span><!-- requirement: core/http -->
<div id="http_status_codes"><h3 class="published-heading">7.5.1.  HTTP status codes</h3><p id="_74f3f505-8346-15d5-fa69-ba348201176f"><a href="#status_codes">Table 10</a> lists the main HTTP status codes that clients should be
prepared to receive.</p>
<p id="_78d0fefa-7544-5f5f-3b88-b41d3b3deba8">This includes, for example, support for specific security schemes or URI
redirection.</p>
<p id="_6867e71f-5920-a5bd-03cd-b8c61541c88f">In addition, other error situations may occur in the transport layer
outside of the server.</p>
<p class="TableTitle" style="text-align:center;">Table 10 — Typical HTTP status codes</p><table class="MsoISOTable" id="status_codes" style="border-width:1px;border-spacing:0;"><colgroup><col style="width: 15%;"/><col style="width: 85%;"/></colgroup><thead><tr><th scope="col" style="font-weight:bold;text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:solid windowtext 1.5pt;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.5pt;">Status code</th><th scope="col" style="font-weight:bold;text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:solid windowtext 1.5pt;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.5pt;">Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:solid windowtext 1.5pt;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>200</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:solid windowtext 1.5pt;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">A successful request.</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>201</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">The request was successful and one or more new resources have being created.</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>204</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">The request was successful but did not generate any content.</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>400</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">The server cannot or will not process the request due to an apparent client error. For example, a query parameter had an incorrect value.</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>401</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">The request requires user authentication. The response includes a <tt>WWW-Authenticate</tt> header field containing a challenge applicable to the requested resource.</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>403</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">The server understood the request, but is refusing to fulfill it. While status code <tt>401</tt> indicates missing or bad authentication, status code <tt>403</tt> indicates that authentication is not the issue, but the client is not authorized to perform the requested operation on the resource.</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>404</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">The requested resource does not exist on the server. For example, a path parameter had an incorrect value.</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>405</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">The request method is not supported. For example, a POST request was submitted, but the resource only supports GET requests.</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>406</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">The <tt>Accept</tt> header submitted in the request did not support any of the media types supported by the server for the requested resource.</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>410</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">The target resource is no longer available at the origin server.</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>429</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time (“rate limiting”).</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">
<tt>500</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;">An internal error occurred in the server.</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.5pt;">
<tt>501</tt>
</td><td style="text-align:left;vertical-align:middle;border-top:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.5pt;">The server does not support the functionality required to fulfill the request.</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p id="_2c6fcc5c-36f4-f48f-a8c2-cf8154b1c493">More specific guidance is provided for each resource, where applicable.</p>
<span id="per_core_additiona-status-codes"></span><!-- permission: core/additional-status-codes -->
<p id="_fd3cabbf-3cc6-c412-3b87-f2733ac2bb44">When a server encounters an error in the processing of a request, it may wish to include information in addition to the status code in the response. Since Web API interactions are often machine-to-machine, a machine-readable report would be preferred. <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7807">RFC 7807</a> addresses this need by providing “Problem Details” response schemas for both JSON and XML.</p>
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_problem-details" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 3</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/problem-details</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p id="_e4deb5c8-0860-c46a-e09e-12a34f0f1480">A server SHOULD include a “Problem Details” report in an error response in accordance with <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7807">RFC 7807</a>.</p></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<div id="_support_for_cross_origin_requests"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc27">7.6.  Support for cross-origin requests</h2><p id="_bde61999-3281-8757-013d-0448bbca37d2">Access to content from a HTML page is by default prohibited for security reasons if the content is located on another host than the webpage (“same-origin policy”). Cross-origin resource sharing is a mechanism that allows restricted resources on a web page to be requested from another domain outside the domain from which the first resource was served. A typical example is a web-application accessing processes and data from multiple servers.</p>
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_cross-origin" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 4</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/cross-origin</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p id="_617befed-dd6c-ef7f-5e1a-2d69bdf93697">If the server is intended to be accessed from the browser, cross-origin
requests SHOULD be supported. Note that support can also be added in a
proxy layer on top of the server.</p></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p id="_7c65487e-b249-54ce-a3f4-88cf952bb47d">Two common mechanisms to support cross-origin requests are:</p>
<ul id="_cf1de783-7677-a3e1-e4db-8f79252630b0">
<li>
<p id="_8bad9d71-009e-15d6-b0a1-f0676a937ff8">
<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-origin_resource_sharing">Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)</a>
</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_2635de25-ce81-bb68-a254-04c9342a286d">
<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSONP">JSONP (JSON with padding)</a>
</p>
</li>
</ul>
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_access-control-expose-headers" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 5</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/access-control-expose-headers</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p id="_cf8e7e58-193a-042f-86d8-ada1542bec40">If the server is intended to be accessed from the browser and if Cross-origin resource sharing is supported, the <tt>Access-Control-Expose-Headers</tt> header SHOULD be used and the header SHOULD contain the value <tt>location</tt> to enable the browser to access the <tt>location</tt> header of the response.</p></td></tr></tbody></table>
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_html" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 6</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/html</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p id="_971c540d-47c6-8c39-1f27-0e3e31532176">To support browsing an implementation of OGC API — Processes with a web browser and to enable search engines to crawl
and index a process, implementations SHOULD consider to support an HTML encoding.</p></td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<div id="sc_limit_parameter"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc28">7.7.  Limit parameter</h2><p id="_9aca8c7a-5c72-70dd-71bb-481dbeb416aa">Several resources defined in this specification (see <a href="#sc_process_list">Retrieve a process list</a>, <a href="#sc_job_list">Retrieve a job list</a>) use the <tt>limit</tt> parameter to control the number of results that are presented in a response.</p>
<ul id="_bc28498c-13f2-54a9-b0bc-d7fafb50b064">
<li>
<p id="_a873f6cc-38ba-3c7d-2d3c-96f89963a1bf">The client can request a limit it is interested in.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_a66adfe1-de0e-9c2d-86a8-e0be4cd40685">The server likely has a default value for the limit, and a maximum limit.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_a39b3ad3-7093-2d60-c5eb-17f3fe2cc58c">If the server has any more results available than it returns (the number it returns is less than or equal to the requested/default/maximum limit) then the server will include a link to the next set of results.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="_95f661ef-4e8a-aa33-27d1-f3c797c3a3e3">So (using the default/maximum values of 10/1000 from the OpenAPI fragment in requirement <a href="#req_core_pl-limit-definition"><tt>/req/core/pl-limit-definition</tt></a> or <a href="#req_job-list_limit-definition"><tt>/req/job-list/limit-definition</tt></a>):</p>
<ul id="_e109ef9b-5b92-29ba-dc19-be98745f119c">
<li>
<p id="_573dc752-eb4c-0efd-ffe6-0fb48324cd15">If you ask for 10 results, you will get 0 to 10 (as requested) and if there are more, a <tt>next</tt> link;</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_af2b747c-1092-1545-7619-a2baa61ac16b">If you don’t specify a limit, you will get 0 to 10 (default) and if there are more, a <tt>next</tt> link;</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_094f1e1d-e9b3-3723-e4bc-4e5fd7093b0b">If you ask for 5000 results, you might get up to 1000 (server-limited) and if there are more, a <tt>next</tt> link;</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_20c8f78f-45ee-f76b-1987-5b3eff41162f">If you follow the next link from the previous response, you might get up to 1000 additional results and if there are more, a <tt>next</tt> link.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="_55d2fb58-e5a5-89f8-21e0-fb40b11f86e5">This document make requirements and recommendations about links in general and the <tt>next</tt> link in particular at the appropriate resource end points.</p>
<p id="next-link-discussion">This document does not mandate any specific implementation approach for the <tt>next</tt> links.</p>
<p id="_d1c39226-11bf-ca8d-9ce0-3b6d0f38580b">An implementation could use opaque links that are managed by the server. It is up to the server to determine how long these links can be dereferenced. Clients should be prepared to receive a 404 response.</p>
<p id="_f398f364-e338-5a7e-8dd3-c05d246e7ed7">Another implementation approach is to use an implementation-specific parameter that specifies the index within the result set from which the server begins presenting results in the response, like <tt>offset</tt> or the <tt>startIndex</tt> parameter that was used in <a href="#WFS20">WFS 2.0</a>.</p>
<p id="_2938dc79-30dd-9b29-338e-a0827fff49fa">The API will return no <tt>next</tt> link, if it has returned all selected results, and the server knows that. However, the server may not be aware that it has already returned all selected results. For example, if the request states <tt>limit=10</tt> and the query to the backend returns 10 results, the server may not know, if there are more results or not (in most cases there will be more results), unless the total number of results is also computed, which may be too costly. The server will then add the next link, and if there are no more results, dereferencing the next link will return an empty results list and no next link. This behavior is consistent with the statements above.</p>
<p id="_10509a3c-95d6-e47f-42c2-5850424ea2db">Clients should not assume that paging is safe against changes to dataset while a client iterates through <tt>next</tt> links. If a server provides opaque links these could be safe and maintain the state during the original request. Using a parameter for the start index, however, will not be safe.</p>
<p id="prev-link-discussion">This document also makes recommendations about include a <tt>prev</tt> link at the appropriate resource end points.  Providing <tt>prev</tt> links supports navigating back and forth between pages, but depending on the implementation approach it may be too complex to implement.</p></div>
<div id="_link_headers"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc29">7.8.  Link headers</h2>
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_link-header" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 7</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/link-header</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;">A</td><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;"><p id="_aa6ea58c-2e01-ab95-b4a8-0dd35796f59d">Links included in payload of responses SHOULD also be included as <tt>Link</tt> headers in the HTTP response according to <a href="#rfc8288">RFC 8288, Clause 3</a>.</p>
<p id="_75653621-1af7-5a59-b7ee-102efa1ffef0">This recommendation does not apply, if there are a large number of links included in a response or a link is not known when the HTTP headers of the response are created.</p></td></tr></tbody></table>
</div>
<div id="sc_process_list"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc30">7.9.  Retrieve a process list</h2><p id="_f3483331-4eaf-f5c8-1248-4e89bf936b63">The following section defines the requirements to retrieve the available processes offered by the server.</p>
<div id="_operation_4"><h3 class="published-heading">7.9.1.  Operation</h3><div id="_process_list"><h4 class="published-heading">7.9.1.1.  Process list</h4>
<span id="req_core_process-list"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-list -->
</div>
<div id="_parameter_limit"><h4 class="published-heading">7.9.1.2.  Parameter <tt>limit</tt></h4><span id="req_core_pl-limit-definition"></span><!-- requirement: core/pl-limit-definition -->
<span id="per_core_limit-default-minimum-maximum"></span><!-- permission: core/limit-default-minimum-maximum -->
<span id="req_core_pl-limit-response"></span><!-- requirement: core/pl-limit-response -->
<span id="per_core_limit-response"></span><!-- permission: core/limit-response --></div></div>
<div id="_response_4"><h3 class="published-heading">7.9.2.  Response</h3><span id="req_job-list_job-list-success"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-list-success -->
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_812639be-c98c-914b-0fa2-e3f52643e724">type: object<br/>required:<br/>  - processes<br/>  - links<br/>properties:<br/>  processes:<br/>    type: array<br/>    items:<br/>      $ref: "processSummary.yaml"<br/>  links:<br/>    type: array<br/>    items:<br/>      $ref: "link.yaml"</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 5 — Schema for the process list</p>
<div class="Note" id="_373934b1-c904-5066-6741-f097be1016df"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  1</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/processList.yaml"><tt>processList.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="schema-processSummary">allOf:<br/>  - $ref: "descriptionType.yaml"<br/>  - type: object<br/>    required:<br/>      - id<br/>      - version<br/>    properties:<br/>      id:<br/>        type: string<br/>      version:<br/>        type: string<br/>      jobControlOptions:<br/>        type: array<br/>        items:<br/>          $ref: "jobControlOptions.yaml"<br/>      outputTransmission:<br/>        type: array<br/>        items:<br/>          $ref: "transmissionMode.yaml"<br/>      links:<br/>        type: array<br/>        items:<br/>          $ref: "link.yaml"</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 6 — Schema for a process summary</p>
<div class="Note" id="_88b9ecfa-e442-3668-799e-98d8d53550f3"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  2</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/processSummary.yaml"><tt>processSummary.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<p id="_398f7f72-a1b0-f7a0-29af-e0bdbef91e2c">(see also: <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/descriptionType.yaml"><tt>descriptionType.yaml</tt></a>).</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="job-control-options-schema">type: string<br/>enum:<br/>  - sync-execute<br/>  - async-execute<br/>  - dismiss</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 7 — Schema for the job control options</p>
<div class="Note" id="_5055c3a2-2b33-54b9-1bd7-da063fb12722"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  3</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/jobControlOptions.yaml"><tt>jobControlOptions.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="transmission-mode-schema">type: string<br/>enum:<br/>  - value<br/>  - reference<br/>default:<br/>  - value</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 8 — Schema for the transmission mode</p>
<div class="Note" id="_3b586f1d-7536-f5dd-8bb0-48e74c0497bb"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  4</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/transmissionMode.yaml"><tt>transmissionMode.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<p id="_a5e6d2d8-febc-81c8-1ddd-71f8fb7a49ed">The number of process summaries returned depends on the server and the parameter <tt>limit.</tt></p>
<p id="_8ee36df1-9195-a548-33ad-ae08e8ceaf43">See the discussion about the <tt>limit</tt> parameter in the <a href="#sc_limit_parameter">Limit parameter</a> section.</p>
<span id="req_core_pl-links"></span><!-- requirement: core/pl-links -->
<p id="_8fcfd7c0-f48f-8d78-b5dc-085a5850ac12">See the discussion about the <tt>next</tt> links in the <a href="#next-link-discussion">Limit parameter</a> section.</p>
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_next-1" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 8</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/next-1</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;">A</td><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;">
<p id="_f8f53dbb-7a10-54ea-7232-41da09bd1645">A <tt>200</tt>-response SHOULD include a link to the next page (relation: <tt>next</tt>) of process summaries, if more process summaries have been selected than returned in the response.</p>
</td></tr></tbody></table>
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_next-2" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 9</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/next-2</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;">A</td><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;">
<p id="_9a7139b1-3afb-6d9a-fd5a-55f4a7af66c3">Dereferencing a next page link (relation: <tt>next</tt>) SHOULD return additional process summaries from the set of selected process summaries that have not yet been returned.</p>
</td></tr></tbody></table>
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_next-3" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 10</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/next-3</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;">A</td><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;">
<p id="_3dad80a2-2c0e-6b00-d44e-18be2117501c">The number of process summaries in a response to dereferencing a next page link (relation: <tt>next</tt>) SHOULD follow the same rules as for the response to the original query and again include a next page link (relation: <tt>next</tt>), if there are more process summaries in the selection that have not yet been returned.</p>
</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p id="_18b4f65e-a118-29f3-8edf-86cc9d14f933">See the discussion about the <tt>prev</tt> link in the  <a href="#prev-link-discussion">Limit parameter</a> section.</p>
<span id="per_core_prev"></span><!-- permission: core/prev -->
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Example  1 — A HTTP GET request for retrieving the list of offered processes encoded as JSON.</p><div class="example" id="_3a42f929-81c0-1ffc-4a6a-a730881d81d4"><pre class="prettyprint" id="_49b24b6f-0402-c9e7-f556-5f03d449161c">GET /processes HTTP/1.1<br/>Host: processing.example.org</pre>
</div>
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Example  2 — A Process list encoded as JSON.</p><div class="example" id="_a1ba41b0-913d-a18c-ddcf-7c24b9b9f49e"><pre class="prettyprint" id="_7ac6fe05-5411-dd6f-4431-5a2ad2bdaea8">{<br/>  "processes": [<br/>    {<br/>	"id": "EchoProcess",<br/>	"title": "EchoProcess",<br/>	"version": "1.0.0",<br/>      "jobControlOptions": [<br/>        "async-execute",<br/>        "sync-execute"<br/>      ],<br/>      "outputTransmission": [<br/>        "value",<br/>        "reference"<br/>      ],<br/>      "links": [<br/>        {<br/>          "href": "https://processing.example.org/oapi-p/processes/EchoProcess",<br/>          "type": "application/json",<br/>          "rel": "self",<br/>          "title": "process description"<br/>        }<br/>      ]<br/>    }<br/>  ],<br/>  "links": [<br/>    {<br/>      "href": "https://processing.example.org/oapi-p/processes?f=json",<br/>      "rel": "self",<br/>      "type": "application/json"<br/>    },<br/>    {<br/>      "href": "https://processing.example.org/oapi-p/processes?f=html",<br/>      "rel": "alternate",<br/>      "type": "text/html"<br/>    }<br/>  ]<br/>}</pre>
</div></div>
<div id="_error_situations_4"><h3 class="published-heading">7.9.3.  Error situations</h3>
<p id="_3b682a8a-10be-9e3d-7e30-fbecbcdf54cc">See <a href="#http_status_codes">Clause 7.5.1</a> for general guidance.</p>
</div></div>
<div id="sc_process_description"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc31">7.10.  Retrieve a process description</h2><p id="_38684aaa-d2ee-e023-273e-0c77173e6767">The following section defines the requirements to retrieve metadata about a process.</p>
<div id="_operation_5"><h3 class="published-heading">7.10.1.  Operation</h3>
<span id="req_core_process"></span><!-- requirement: core/process -->
</div>
<div id="_response_5"><h3 class="published-heading">7.10.2.  Response</h3><span id="req_core_process-success"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-success -->
<p id="_c7d9843e-53ec-1bb0-5993-262c3a69e55a">The <a href="#rc_core">Core</a> does not mandate the use of a specific process description
to specify the interface of a process.  That said, the <a href="#rc_core">Core</a>
requirements class makes the following recommendation:</p>
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_ogc-process-description" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 11</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/ogc-process-description</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p id="_051dc2f8-d821-e5c5-9ba3-41bd39666456">Implementations SHOULD consider supporting the <a href="#ogc_process_description">OGC process description</a>.</p></td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<div id="_error_situations_5"><h3 class="published-heading">7.10.3.  Error situations</h3><p id="_53e70cf9-6f0c-9fa6-2be7-8b2edd2dc6e3">See <a href="#http_status_codes">Clause 7.5.1</a> for general guidance.</p>
<span id="req_core_process-exception-no-such-process"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-exception/no-such-process --></div></div>
<div id="sc_create_job"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc32">7.11.  Execute a process</h2><p id="_c392e627-85c9-00e3-3c71-8bf16b727513">This section describes the requirements for executing a process.</p>
<p id="_b0c4ecea-513f-ec8a-5ec2-15059ecaf200">Depending on the description of the <a href="#sc_process_description">process</a> and the <a href="#sc_execution_mode">negotiated process execution mode</a>, process execution may result in the creation of a <a href="#sc_retrieve_job_results">job resource</a>.</p>
<div id="_operation_6"><h3 class="published-heading">7.11.1.  Operation</h3>
<span id="req_core_process-execute-op"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-op -->
</div>
<div id="_request_body"><h3 class="published-heading">7.11.2.  Request body</h3><div id="_content_schema"><h4 class="published-heading">7.11.2.1.  Content schema</h4><span id="req_core_process-execute-request"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-request -->
<pre class="prettyprint" id="execute-request-body">type: object<br/>properties:<br/>  inputs:<br/>    additionalProperties:<br/>      oneOf:<br/>        - $ref: "inlineOrRefData.yaml"<br/>        - type: array<br/>          items:<br/>            $ref: "inlineOrRefData.yaml"<br/>  outputs:<br/>    additionalProperties:<br/>      $ref: "output.yaml"<br/>  response:<br/>    type: string<br/>    enum:<br/>      - raw<br/>      - document<br/>    default:<br/>      - raw<br/>  subscriber:<br/>    $ref: "subscriber.yaml"</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 9 — Schema for execute</p>
<div class="Note" id="_c5ee4f68-cc7e-91c9-6533-2080a6814b44"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  1</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/execute.yaml"><tt>execute.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="inline-or-ref-data">oneOf:<br/>  - $ref: "inputValueNoObject.yaml"<br/>  - $ref: "qualifiedInputValue.yaml"<br/>  - $ref: "link.yaml"</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 10 — Schema for an in-line or referenced process input value</p>
<div class="Note" id="_2db690ca-543f-1a15-d316-5f1183b89a09"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  2</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/inlineOrRefData.yaml"><tt>inlineOrRefData.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<p id="_1e2bc9e2-ca9d-cd29-438a-e4656ad04a3b">(see also: <a href="#input-value-noobject-schema">inputValueNoObject.yaml</a>, <a href="#qualified-value-schema">qualifiedInputValue.yaml</a>, <a href="#link-schema">link.yaml</a>)</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="output-schema">type: object<br/>properties:<br/>  format:<br/>    $ref: "format.yaml"<br/>  transmissionMode:<br/>    $ref: "transmissionMode.yaml"</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 11 — Schema for a process output</p>
<div class="Note" id="_7392fa67-42b4-08b9-3e80-d41912a5d6b4"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  3</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/output.yaml"><tt>output.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<p id="_1519beee-cffd-65c0-2808-5009109ba282">(see also: <a href="#format-schema">format.yaml</a>, <a href="#tx-mode-schema">transmissionMode.yaml</a>)</p></div>
<div id="sc_process_inputs"><h4 class="published-heading">7.11.2.2.  Process inputs</h4><p id="_e4da91ae-10e3-0f13-10b4-288f5071d1d6">
<b>
<i>Overview:</i>
</b>
</p>
<p id="_be0d1fa2-e9c9-e00d-fe02-a87b661541df">Each process input is a name/value pair that appears in the <tt>inputs</tt> section of
an execute request.</p>
<p id="_841ff2f6-c5cd-4cdd-8cb4-878edf88f0e1">The name of each input is its identifier as specified by the input’s definition in the <a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a>.</p>
<p id="_4178323c-85ec-d330-6345-7a2a9fc6b5b5">Process input values in an execute request can be specified in-line or by reference.</p>
<span id="req_core_process-execute-inputs"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-inputs -->
<p id="_70b1b18c-0f9e-08dc-8856-f26418d1d17e">As shown in <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/inlineOrRefData.yaml">inlineOrRefData.yaml</a>, a process input value that is specified in-line in an execute request can be:</p>
<ul id="_2f9b76e9-47bc-2148-7e81-8e117bbf5d26">
<li>
<p id="_c7da6ac2-8871-9b09-b3ca-84369227d214">a simple literal value,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_d6a5b5d2-bd36-b7ce-b626-052bc53ab306">an array,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_493460aa-12b1-a7d2-5fe6-6afa10dd747e">a qualified value,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_66486304-0a8c-d56e-6410-a31dc6e0174b">a binary value,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_f9b32c4c-3df6-0982-1650-dba7a6eae1cc">or a bounding box.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="simple-literals">
<b>
<i>Simple literal values:</i>
</b>
</p>
<p id="_3f48e15f-e8a3-df67-3ba5-01a344d8526e">A simple literal value can be a string, number, integer or Boolean.</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="input-value-noobject-schema">oneOf:<br/>  - type: string<br/>  - type: number<br/>  - type: integer<br/>  - type: boolean<br/>  - type: array<br/>  - $ref: "binaryInputValue.yaml"<br/>  - $ref: "bbox.yaml"</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 12 — Schema for a simple literal value</p>
<div class="Note" id="_dca56716-5cfc-211a-7a18-881281c2551f"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  1</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/inputValueNoObject.yaml"><tt>inputValueNoObject.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<p id="_1eeeec78-06ba-e16b-5a5e-efd2364cce06">(see also: <a href="#binary-input-value-schema">binaryInputValue.yaml</a>, <a href="#bbox-schema">bbox.yaml</a>)</p>
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Example  1 — Simple literal value examples.</p><div class="example" id="_bbd29a14-389f-6c65-e6bf-df1d11fc9d7e"><p id="_d7dbc4e6-8181-2881-bc70-4586c159e898">A string literal:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_1e6af2ed-21e8-ff05-9c62-983e86b39e01">"stringInput": "String value"</pre>
<p id="_334e1107-cde4-7c15-bb40-2ddad8b86ea2">A date string:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_59997477-7747-cfb0-36dc-22dded34464f">"dateInput": "2021-05-24T20:40:13-05:00"</pre>
<p id="_a89d44d4-63a6-37ac-03a1-7b83e1632889">A number:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_cef6be83-3b69-62a0-001f-01145f6b9c5d">"numberInput": 3.14159</pre>
<p id="_07266226-8811-d37a-3bdf-f7438df19abd">An integer:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_4136abbd-3395-40db-3f5c-f6e494b53538">"integerInput": 10</pre>
<p id="_96a36047-e285-78ed-9abe-23dff4ecd6f1">A Boolean:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_eb0dbb8b-785a-6f72-ae62-4fc2b37678ea">"booleanInput": true</pre>
</div>
<p id="arrays">
<b>
<i>Array of values:</i>
</b>
</p>
<p id="_304347ab-8fae-d570-de76-1ca0db11d185">Array elements, as per <a href="#inline-or-ref-data">inlineOrRefData.yaml</a>, can be:</p>
<ul id="_4f20b9ac-7eea-8f37-b459-39f892452606">
<li>
<p id="_c8f17412-6d3a-4780-4176-fa0d1aa77212"><a href="#simple-literals">simple literals</a>,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_8eb56670-df5b-c935-cfb1-39f87ae4fff4">embedded arrays,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_6c4c59a6-ecf7-425d-7eaf-ae24ceb73232"><a href="#qualified-value">qualified values</a>,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_5cc0b90d-f6dd-e63a-7ff7-ed821e076521"><a href="#binary-value">binary values</a>,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_4d4b756e-0baf-8e16-0b42-7c767a3a8db2"><a href="#bounding-box-value">bounding box values</a>,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_71408aa0-c2ee-ba69-5285-8ae813b28660">or references to values using <a href="#link-schema">links</a>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<span id="req_core_process-execute-input-array"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-input-array -->
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Example  2 — Array value examples.</p><div class="example" id="_60c99977-ece8-0774-c12b-9b823ce2c043"><p id="_dfc0a892-ab4d-c136-9876-bec24b8d24ef">An array of simple values:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_5c447d4b-3ca8-62da-4346-3aab16f38e63">"arrayOfSimpleValues": [1, 2, 4, 10, 7]</pre>
<p id="_e1531324-6464-0fad-2fd9-1f7d5d6b8728">An array with a single simple value:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_ac89a34d-9434-c202-89de-96468bff4ef0">"arrayOfSimpleValues": ["a"]</pre>
<p id="_54f5295d-0bd4-4b21-5670-7cff9bd68d62">An array of arrays of simple values:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_6dcd07cc-9b95-fdd7-b9c9-c8094c3b2cf4">"arrayOfArrays": [[1,2,3,4], ["a","b","c","d"]]</pre>
<p id="_81cd5557-b1d0-895a-7939-0cc26e6c3922">An array of objects values:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_1327a2c8-9eef-4c48-7de0-39d690be4f40">"arrayOfQualifiedValues": [<br/>  {<br/>    "value": {<br/>      "measurement": 10.3,<br/>      "uom": "m",<br/>      "reference": "https://ucum.org/ucum-essence.xml"<br/>    }<br/>  },<br/>  {<br/>    "value": {<br/>      "measurement": 10.5,<br/>      "uom": "m",<br/>      "reference": "https://ucum.org/ucum-essence.xml"<br/>    }<br/>  },<br/>  {<br/>    "value": {<br/>      "measurement": 10.9,<br/>      "uom": "m",<br/>      "reference": "https://ucum.org/ucum-essence.xml"<br/>    }<br/>  },...<br/>],</pre>
<div class="Note" id="_78c5f8b8-b602-331f-962e-c95bbd7f4d4e"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  2</span>  In an execute request, as per requirement <a href="#req_core_process-execute-input-inline-object">/req/core/process-execute-input-inline-object</a>, object values must be encoded as <a href="#qualified-value">qualified values</a> to prevent unintended ambiguity with the built-in value types (i.e. <a href="#bounding-box-value">bounding boxes</a>, <a href="#link-schema">links</a> or <a href="#qualified-value">qualified values</a>).</p></div></div>
<p id="qualified-value">
<b>
<i>Qualified values:</i>
</b>
</p>
<p id="_32f14110-8a1f-0a6f-7dfc-c33235380956">A qualified value is a <a href="#input-value-schema">value</a> that can be optionally qualified with a <tt>format</tt> parameter.</p>
<p id="_95d43027-a44d-b9d6-359d-eee7bc4c6a4c">Qualified values can be used to encode process input values that, according to their definition in the <a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a>, can be of multiple media types.  The <tt>format</tt> parameter is used to identify the specific media type being provided as the process input.</p>
<p id="_b0f7f3c8-8137-b14a-793d-068503faa743">Qualified values can also be used to encode object-valued process inputs in order to avoid ambiguity with the built-in value schemas defined in this standard (i.e. <a href="#bounding-box-value">bbox.yaml</a>, <a href="#link-schema">link.yaml</a> or <a href="#qualified-value">qualifiedInputValue.yaml</a> itself).</p>
<p id="_d32d57d0-e605-4feb-ba35-21ab0d61fa57">The actual <i>value</i> in a qualified value object is specified using the <tt>value</tt> key.  The value of the <tt>value</tt> key is an instance of <a href="#input-value-schema">inputValue.yaml</a>.</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="qualified-value-schema">allOf:<br/>  - $ref: "format.yaml"<br/>  - type: object<br/>    required:<br/>      - value<br/>    properties:<br/>      value:<br/>        $ref: "inputValue.yaml"</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 13 — Schema for a qualified value</p>
<div class="Note" id="_df59421b-c16c-cace-a006-dd04ca33271b"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  3</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/qualifiedInputValue.yaml"><tt>qualifiedInputValue.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="format-schema">type: object<br/>properties:<br/>  mediaType:<br/>    type: string<br/>  encoding:<br/>    type: string<br/>  schema:<br/>    oneOf:<br/>      - type: string<br/>        format: url<br/>      - type: object</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 14 — Schema for a format qualifier</p>
<div class="Note" id="_7feabb73-79c7-ffd3-3f9f-4bf50cc505e0"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  4</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/format.yaml"><tt>format.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="input-value-schema">oneOf:<br/>  - $ref: "inputValueNoObject.yaml"<br/>  - type: object</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 15 — Schema of a process input value</p>
<div class="Note" id="_96c8b38c-7d94-eb5f-e3f9-40d4f4a9a834"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  5</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/inputValue.yaml"><tt>inputValue.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<p id="_5ce2d25a-9d5f-7061-af9e-4a23b7c9ff39">(see also: <a href="#input-value-noobject-schema">inputValueNoObject.yaml</a>)</p>
<span id="req_core_process-execute-input-inline-object"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-input-inline-object -->
<span id="req_core_process-execute-input-inline-mixed"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-input-mixed-type -->
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Example  3 — Qualified value examples.</p><div class="example" id="_682fbddb-8732-5eb7-bb73-5e2f3a8518e4"><p id="_100f57f3-cd57-2b57-000f-49743ec74cb0">An example of a complex process input value.</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_200bb087-67ae-da87-bba8-3c0e89860f40">"complexObjectInput": {<br/>  "value": {<br/>    "property1": "value1",<br/>    "property2": "value2",<br/>    "property3": "value3"<br/>  }<br/>}</pre>
<p id="_8cb4dc5d-0701-ab8e-425a-2063ee757aca">In this second example, the property, <tt>geometryInput</tt> has a cardinality of greater than 1 and value instances can be one of a number of enumerated media types.  The schema of <tt>geometryInput</tt> from the <a href="#ogc_process_description">OGC process description</a> for the process might be:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_b6f7d5ce-773a-b9d7-26d1-1e5702b1df07">"geometryInput": {<br/>  "title": "Geometry input",<br/>  "description": "This is an example of a geometry input.  In this case the geometry can be expressed as a GML of GeoJSON geometry.",<br/>  "minOccurs": 2,<br/>  "maxOccurs": 5,<br/>  "schema": {<br/>    "oneOf": [<br/>      {<br/>        "type": "string",<br/>        "contentMediaType": "application/gml+xml; version=3.2",<br/>        "contentSchema": "http://schemas.opengis.net/gml/3.2.1/geometryBasic2d.xsd"<br/>      },<br/>      {<br/>        "$ref": "http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/features/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/geometryGeoJSON.json"<br/>      }<br/>    ]<br/>  }<br/>},</pre>
<p id="_f4660abc-fe02-3678-ee6c-28cffa729857">and an instance of this process input in an execute request might be:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_41d4f3ef-94db-a90b-4ed3-b00b21abc2a2">"geometryInputs": [<br/>  {<br/>    "value": "&lt;gml:Polygon gml:id=\"GID1\" srsName=\"urn:ogc:def:crs:OGC::CRS84\"&gt;&lt;gml:exterior&gt;&lt;gml:LinearRing&gt;&lt;gml:posList&gt;-77.024519 38.810529 -77.024635 38.810973 -77.024704 38.810962 -77.024776 38.811239 -77.024957 38.81121 -77.024905 38.811012 -77.024905 38.811012 -77.024865 38.810857 -77.025024 38.810832 -77.025071 38.811012 -77.025203 38.810992 -77.02506 38.810444 -77.024519 38.810529&lt;/gml:posList&gt;&lt;/gml:LinearRing&gt;&lt;/gml:exterior&gt;&lt;/gml:Polygon&gt;",<br/>    "mediaType": "application/gml+xml; version=3.2"<br/>  },<br/>  {<br/>    "value": {<br/>      "type": "Polygon",<br/>      "coordinates": [[[ -176.5814819, -44.10896301 ],<br/>                       [ -176.5818024, -44.10964584 ],<br/>                       [ -176.5844116, -44.11236572 ],<br/>                       [ -176.5935974, -44.11021805 ],<br/>                       [ -176.5973511, -44.10743332 ],<br/>                       [ -176.5950928, -44.10562134 ],<br/>                       [ -176.5858459, -44.1043396  ],<br/>                       [ -176.5811157, -44.10667801 ],<br/>                       [ -176.5814819, -44.10896301 ]]]<br/>    },<br/>    "mediaType": "application/geo+json"<br/>  }<br/>]</pre>
<p id="_222fd525-9173-a83f-c7f9-f1804d7c4b28">In this case, the <tt>mediaType</tt> parameter is used to indicate the specific type of geometry being passed as input in each case; GML Polygon for the first element of the array and GeoJSON Polygon for the second element.</p></div>
<p id="binary-value">
<b>
<i>Binary values:</i>
</b>
</p>
<p id="_1f8c4241-9457-c9b6-e9e4-0798188a3f79">In some cases, for example in order to pass through firewalls, binary input values need to be encoded in-line in an execute request as a string.</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="binary-input-value-schema">type: string<br/>format: byte</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 16 — Schema for an in-line binary value</p>
<div class="Note" id="_fc883097-5bf3-eef5-57c3-c746961be770"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  6</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/binaryInputValue.yaml"><tt>binaryInputValue.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<span id="req_core_process-execute-input-inline-binary"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-input-inline-binary -->
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Example  4 — Binary value examples.</p><div class="example" id="_a8f30fe9-7a22-76a9-066e-70f325baf8f6"><p id="_264dcd7d-6850-1140-2fbb-e92c9bfda318">This is an example of an image process input whose media type is defined in the
<a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a>.  The schema definition for this process input might be:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_b9846ef5-c333-c694-b53b-4797c812e592">"schema": {<br/>  "type": "string",<br/>  "contentEncoding": "binary",<br/>  "contentMediaType": "application/tiff; application=geotiff"<br/>}</pre>
<p id="_33099b6c-9642-4a09-b0b2-7cfaf2c7b9f0">and an example instance value in an execute request might be:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_d9fb9437-1117-569e-6a90-c7281e977cbf">"imageInput": "R0lGODdhNAHCAfcAAAcHDD+Gs4sLDQpDaqGFdaHE54dJPEoECUlGRteKgcdITgokG4hoVkpY\ngNzHwKKkqOLm7RRjlEgpHU9iZ44lHQYqVdmki6doVmhHOMOIeJG20HiDjCcKBglIeadISrso\nJGooFNbN2d2qr8aljyklHwQJQkdvkWaKxIdrb442LidLeGhMTp6LkeP1+Kh3aiUuVAoUHmlu\ngkcwNYdZRmkJDYGcsDFokElVYyk1NsWWhLEPDtmQldrUyoyFhrjo+Nna5d+4tMGstspoXgc4\n...qgu7sSu7qbtCs2u7t6u6rLsrp4u7veu76eO6vyu8w0u8xWu8x4u8yau8shu8y+u8zwu90Su9\n00u91Wu914u92au928u9whsQADs="</pre>
<div class="Note" id="_ec49a73c-9a60-d77e-2e4a-025d96cd558e"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  7</span>  Even though the schema indicates that the input type is <tt>binary</tt>, when the input value is encoded in-line in an execute request, as per requirement <a href="#req_core_process-execute-input-inline-binary">/req/core/process-execute-input-inline-binary</a>, the binary value is encoded as base64-encoded string.</p></div>
<p id="_58f5c976-2c0f-419c-3ddf-240af8cc0ec8">In this second example, the image input can be one of a number of value types denoted in JSON Schema by the use of the <tt>oneOf[]</tt> construct.  An example schema for this a process input might be:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_9bacea51-9dea-0412-b68b-8b5e357e7bdd">"schema": {<br/>  "oneOf": [<br/>    {<br/>      "type": "string",<br/>      "contentEncoding": "binary",<br/>      "contentMediaType": "application/tiff; application=geotiff"<br/>    },<br/>    {<br/>      "type": "string",<br/>      "contentEncoding": "binary",<br/>      "contentMediaType": "application/jp2"<br/>    }<br/>  ]<br/>}</pre>
<p id="_56c3ad60-6f6e-bb0e-7fa9-f305af395459">and a JPEG2000 instance example in an execute request might be:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_34e7b43a-9ee0-6bc5-74ef-cacf132bb3ae">{<br/>  "value": "VBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAABvwAAAa4CAYAAABMB35kAAABhGlDQ1BJQ0MgcHJvZmlsZQAA\nKJF9kT1Iw0AcxV9TpSL1A+xQxCFDdbIgKuKoVShChVArtOpgcumH0KQhSXFxFFwLDn4sVh1c\nnHV1cBUEwQ8QNzcnRRcp8X9JoUWMB8f9eHfvcfcOEOplplkdY4Cm22Y6mRCzuRUx9IogouhH\n ... \nj3Z5mX7/PCPVRJV92rpHK24xcJrzk20+tkeYlCPqcZNO3Lpni1OJWatPCcmgGDEqx7Om6lfa\nppM4k4BTe9+bsn3L9/9/yWhA0PwQGW8ipCZsnZt9lsdrYEM8z/M8z/M8z/M8z/M8z/MzLWY1\nAAAACUlEQVQ871H6P6JI+TxS5Wn2AAAAAElFTkSuQmCC",<br/>  "mediaType": "application/jp2"<br/>}</pre>
</div>
<p id="bounding-box-value">
<b>
<i>Bounding box values:</i>
</b>
</p>
<p id="_3ed660de-d88a-426e-5da7-2bf80c7fd85d">A process input value instance can be a bounding box.</p>
<span id="req-creation-input-inline-bbox"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-input-inline-bbox -->
<pre class="prettyprint" id="bbox-schema">type: object<br/>required:<br/>  - bbox<br/>properties:<br/>  bbox:<br/>    type: array<br/>    oneOf:<br/>      - minItems: 4<br/>        maxItems: 4<br/>      - minItems: 6<br/>        maxItems: 6<br/>    items:<br/>      type: number<br/>  crs:<br/>    type: string<br/>    format: uri<br/>    default: "http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/OGC/1.3/CRS84"<br/>    enum:<br/>      - "http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/OGC/1.3/CRS84"<br/>      - "http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/OGC/0/CRS84h"</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 17 — Schema for a bounding box value</p>
<div class="Note" id="_e0af6ef2-2acf-779a-76b0-f5788da8ec44"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  8</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/bbox.yaml"><tt>bbox.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<p id="_4789f1d6-9292-6773-53df-3131b34ab4b0">This schema is meant to be a template for defining bounding box process inputs. If the specified <tt>default</tt> and <tt>enum</tt> are suitable for your purposes then you can reference this file directly in your process description.</p>
<span id="per_core_creation-input-inline-bbox"></span><!-- permission: core/process-execute-input-inline-bbox--published-permission-6 -->
<p id="_c64a052f-3c5c-d528-485b-5ba72cf85b87">
<b>
<i>Input validation</i>
</b>
</p>
<p id="_2fb2d9f0-1c40-c4e8-081c-aa894b506482">Process inputs in an execute request and the corresponding process input definition in the <a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a> have a validation relationship.  That is to say, that the schema of a process input definition from the <a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a> can be used to validate the component of the corresponding process input value in an execute request that is an instance of <a href="#input-value-schema">inputValue.yaml</a>.</p>
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;"></p><div class="example" id="_1a6ab68b-535d-ed5f-56b1-4bbfe971a852"><p id="_23dac6a2-4273-dad9-ac13-4aa05e77131c">Consider a process input named <tt>complexObjectInput</tt> with the following definition from an <a href="#ogc_process_description">OGC process description</a>:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_7f68656a-ca66-13f2-5d5b-c0db4e15e882">"complexObjectInput": {<br/>  "title": "Complex Object Input Example",<br/>  "description": "This is an example of a complex object input.",<br/>  "schema": {<br/>    "type": "object",<br/>    "required": [<br/>      "property1",<br/>      "property5"<br/>    ],<br/>    "properties": {<br/>      "property1": {<br/>        "type": "string"<br/>      },<br/>      "property2": {<br/>        "type": "string",<br/>        "format": "uri"<br/>      },<br/>      "property3": {<br/>        "type": "number"<br/>      },<br/>      "property4": {<br/>        "type": "string",<br/>        "format": "dateTime"<br/>      },<br/>      "property5": {<br/>        "type": "boolean"<br/>      }<br/>    }<br/>  }<br/>}</pre>
<p id="_9ac000b4-a80d-2d40-1acb-80ed17161a30">and the following instance in an execute request:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_e558e819-4a97-4f10-d8f1-2f10c05c48e1">"inputs": [<br/>  .<br/>  .<br/>  .<br/>  "complexObjectInput": {<br/>    "value": {<br/>      "property1": "value1",<br/>      "property2": "value2",<br/>      "property3": "value5"<br/>    }<br/>  },<br/>  .<br/>  .<br/>  .<br/>]</pre>
<p id="_b337f0f4-e3ad-a299-3635-65aae53ad5f9">The process input value in this execute request is an instance of a <a href="#qualified-value">qualified value</a>.</p>
<p id="_10560188-a550-e04e-22ed-563779b6f63a">For the purposes of validation, the server need only validate the component of the <a href="#qualified-value">qualified value</a> that is an instance of <a href="#input-value-schema">inputValue.yaml</a> against the <tt>schema</tt> fragment from the <a href="#ogc_process_description">OGC process description</a>.  Specifically, the validation target is:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="_435ff0bf-7436-56bd-c186-d3419ca25784">{<br/>  "property1": "value1",<br/>  "property2": "value2",<br/>  "property3": "value5"<br/>}</pre>
<div class="Note" id="_557406fb-e1df-8abe-c251-67c9d7fb51bd"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE  9</span>  This example makes use of an <a href="#ogc_process_description">OGC process description</a>.  However, any other process description vocabulary may be used and applied, for the purpose of validation, in a similar manner.</p></div></div>
<span id="req_core_process-execute-input-validation"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-input-validation --></div>
<div id="sc_execution_mode"><h4 class="published-heading">7.11.2.3.  Execution mode</h4><p id="_931fedc3-ce44-2f3c-5236-719f7c47e177">A process may be executed synchronously or asynchronously.</p>
<p id="_c7de38d7-4949-4305-ad5c-fab0a6cd68bc">In which of these two modes a server responds is a function of the job control options specified in the <a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a> and the presence or absence of the HTTP <tt>Prefer</tt> header (<a href="http://tools.ietf.org/rfc/rfc7240.txt">IETF RFC 7240</a>).</p>
<span id="req_core_process-execute-default-execution-mode"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-default-execution-mode -->
<span id="req_core_process-execute-auto-execution-mode"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-auto-execution-mode -->
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_process-execute-honor-prefer" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 12</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/process-execute-honor-prefer</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;">A</td><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;">
<p id="_b17d5814-714e-88f1-fac9-19bd833cb84a">If an execute request is accompanied with the HTTP <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7240#section-2"><tt>Prefer</tt></a> header asserting a <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7240#section-4.1"><tt>respond-async</tt></a> preference, then the server SHOULD honor that preference and response asynchronously if, according to the job control options in the <a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a>, the process can be executed asynchronously.</p>
</td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;">B</td><td class="recommend" style="vertical-align:top;">
<p id="_5a57370f-28bb-2104-ccb3-89c690bedd83">If an execute request is accompanied with the HTTP <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7240#section-2"><tt>Prefer</tt></a> header asserting a <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7240#section-4.3"><tt>wait</tt></a> preference, then the server SHOULD honor that preference in the decision to execute the process asynchronously if, according to the job control options in the <a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a>, the process can be executed asynchronously.</p>
</td></tr></tbody></table>
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_process-execute-handle-prefer" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 13</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/process-execute-handle-prefer</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p id="_0f792e89-235d-c807-0b27-813d6b7f7fd4">A client that accompanies an execute request with the HTTP <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7240#section-2"><tt>Prefer</tt></a> header asserting a <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7240#section-4.1"><tt>respond-async</tt></a> preference and/or a <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7240#section-4.3"><tt>wait</tt></a> preference SHOULD be prepared to receive either an asynchronous or a synchronous response.</p></td></tr></tbody></table>
<table class="recommend" id="rec_core_process-execute-preference-applied" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;"><thead><tr><th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;"><p class="RecommendationTitle">Recommendation 14</p></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p>/rec/core/process-execute-preference-applied</p></td></tr><tr><td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;"><p id="_1daed5f5-d51b-bcc3-703f-c4287ec28536">If an execute request is accompanied with the HTTP <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7240#section-2"><tt>Prefer</tt></a> header then, in the <a href="#sc_execute_response">response</a>, servers SHOULD include the HTTP <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7240#section-3"><tt>Preference-Applied</tt></a> response header as an indication as to which <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7240#section-2">‘Prefer`</a> tokens were honoured by the server.</p></td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<div id="sc_response_parameter"><h4 class="published-heading">7.11.2.4.  Response type</h4><p id="_cd942e01-743d-dafe-0731-4caaf09f86f8">The <tt>response</tt> parameter selects the form used to present processing results.</p>
<ul id="_e7c2d005-ff44-82a1-d363-a5057d4b3719">
<li>
<p id="_a2d9495f-a0c0-ac3b-d718-7e0fdc7b0aee">A <tt>response</tt> value of <tt>document</tt> indicates that the server should generate a response document (see <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/results.yaml">results.yaml</a>) that contains each of the requested process outputs.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_e874d66b-cb2b-2ce5-5ca9-e9c3b1696324">A <tt>response</tt> value of <tt>raw</tt> indicates that the server should present the process responses in their native form without the use of a containing document.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="_5a433f36-fb64-9cd7-182a-64e942ccf566">The default value, if the parameter is not specified is <tt>raw</tt>.</p></div>
<div id="sc_process_outputs"><h4 class="published-heading">7.11.2.5.  Process outputs</h4><p id="_f29b5abe-ee01-8695-867d-6133977f8f1b">
<b>
<i>Overview:</i>
</b>
</p>
<p id="_50cc9cef-87ac-0a0e-7e89-707368e70bf7">Each process output is a named object that appears in the <tt>outputs</tt> section of
an <a href="#execute-request-body">execute request</a>. The name of each output is its identifier as specified by the output’s definition in the <a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a>.</p>
<p id="_45d55f54-334c-a0fb-6e9a-4240bd9573ce">
<b>
<i>Default outputs</i>
</b>
</p>
<span id="req_core_process-execute-default-outputs"></span><!-- requirement: core/process-execute-default-outputs -->
<p id="_d99a06a2-045e-1e84-b78d-51af129a43d1">
<b>
<i>Output value transmission mode</i>
</b>
</p>
<p id="_1fbd6a0d-2857-005c-41fe-266a9637fbc8">Like inputs, output values can be transmitted in-line in a result document or referenced using a <a href="#link-schema">link</a>.  The <tt>transmissionMode</tt> parameter in the execute request controls how the server <a href="#sc_execute_response">responds</a>.</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="tx-mode-schema">type: string<br/>enum:<br/>  - value<br/>  - reference<br/>default:<br/>  - value</pre><p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 18 — Schema for the transmission mode</p>
<div class="Note" id="_62b3828c-2387-9da7-5e44-f685b82be7a1"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE</span>  This schema can also be obtained from <a href="http://schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/processes/part1/1.0/openapi/schemas/transmissionMode.yaml"><tt>transmissionMode.yaml</tt></a>.</p></div>
<p id="_9aeb4f5b-1f56-dfeb-1562-2c44a982b9e1">
<b>
<i>Output value format</i>
</b>
</p>
<p id="_31cf7c46-7434-a954-6263-949008f48461">A process output can be defined in the <a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a> as being of one or more media types.   In cases where a specific output can be presented in one of a number of media types, the <tt>format</tt> parameter in the <a href="#output-schema">execute request</a> can be used to indicate the format that should be used to present the process output value in the server’s <a href="#sc_execute_response">response</a>.</p></div></div>
<div id="_example"><h3 class="published-heading">7.11.3.  Example</h3>
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Example  — An execute request.</p><div class="example" id="_67929a65-0878-5d52-47d2-61df99d3917f"><pre class="prettyprint" id="_a489768e-6f02-7ab9-d530-5ab806d2a25c">{<br/>  "inputs": {<br/>    "stringInput": "Value2",<br/>    "measureInput": {<br/>      "value": {<br/>        "measurement": 10.3,<br/>        "uom": "m",<br/>        "reference": "https://ucum.org/ucum-essence.xml"<br/>      }<br/>    },<br/>    "dateInput": "2021-03-06T07:21:00",<br/>    "doubleInput": 3.14159,<br/>    "arrayInput": [1,2,3,4,5,6],<br/>    "complexObjectInput": {<br/>      "value": {<br/>        "property1": "value1",<br/>        "property2": "value2",<br/>        "property5": true<br/>      }<br/>    },<br/>    "geometryInput": [<br/>      {<br/>        "value": "&lt;gml:Polygon gml:id=\"GID1\" srsName=\"urn:ogc:def:crs:OGC::CRS84\"&gt;&lt;gml:exterior&gt;&lt;gml:LinearRing&gt;&lt;gml:posList&gt;-77.024519 38.810529 -77.024635 38.810973 -77.024704 38.810962 -77.024776 38.811239 -77.024957 38.81121 -77.024905 38.811012 -77.024905 38.811012 -77.024865 38.810857 -77.025024 38.810832 -77.025071 38.811012 -77.025203 38.810992 -77.02506 38.810444 -77.024519 38.810529&lt;/gml:posList&gt;&lt;/gml:LinearRing&gt;&lt;/gml:exterior&gt;&lt;/gml:Polygon&gt;",<br/>        "mediaType": "application/gml+xml; version=3.2"<br/>      },<br/>      {<br/>        "value": {<br/>          "type": "Polygon",<br/>          "coordinates": [[[ -176.5814819, -44.10896301 ],<br/>                           [ -176.5818024, -44.10964584 ],<br/>                           [ -176.5844116, -44.11236572 ],<br/>                           [ -176.5935974, -44.11021805 ],<br/>                           [ -176.5973511, -44.10743332 ],<br/>                           [ -176.5950928, -44.10562134 ],<br/>                           [ -176.5858459, -44.1043396  ],<br/>                           [ -176.5811157, -44.10667801 ],<br/>                           [ -176.5814819, -44.10896301 ]]]<br/>        }<br/>      }<br/>    ],<br/>    "boundingBoxInput": {<br/>      "bbox": [ 51.9, 7, 52, 7.1 ],<br/>      "crs": "http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/OGC/1.3/CRS84"<br/>    },<br/>    "imagesInput": [<br/>      {<br/>        "href": "https://www.someserver.com/ogcapi/Daraa/collections/Daraa_DTED/styles/Topographic/coverage?...",<br/>        "type": "application/tiff; application=geotiff"<br/>      },<br/>      {<br/>         "value": "VBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAABvwAAAa4CAYAAABMB35kAAABhGlDQ1BJQ0MgcHJvZmlsZQAA\nKJF9kT1Iw0AcxV9TpSL1A+xQxCFDdbIgKuKoVShChVArtOpgcumH0KQhSXFxFFwLDn4sVh1c\nnHV1cBUEwQ8QNzcnRRcp8X9JoUWMB8f9eHfvcfcOEOplplkdY4Cm22Y6mRCzuRUx9IogouhH\n ... \nj3Z5mX7/PCPVRJV92rpHK24xcJrzk20+tkeYlCPqcZNO3Lpni1OJWatPCcmgGDEqx7Om6lfa\nppM4k4BTe9+bsn3L9/9/yWhA0PwQGW8ipCZsnZt9lsdrYEM8z/M8z/M8z/M8z/M8z/MzLWY1\nAAAACUlEQVQ871H6P6JI+TxS5Wn2AAAAAElFTkSuQmCC",<br/>         "encoding": "base64",<br/>         "mediaType": "application/jp2"<br/>      }<br/>    ],<br/>    "featureCollectionInput": {<br/>      "value": "&lt;?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?&gt;&lt;FeatureCollection xmlns=\"http://schemas.myserver.com/namespaces/null\" xmlns:gml=\"http://www.opengis.net/gml/3.2\" xmlns:xsi=\"http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance\" xsi:schemaLocation=\"http://schemas.myserver.com/namespaces/null https://www.pvretano.com/myserver/ogcapi/daraa/schema?f=GML32&amp;amp;collectionids=TransportationGroundCrv http://www.opengis.net/gml/3.2 http://schemas.opengis.net/schemas/gml/3.2.1/gml.xsd\"&gt;...",<br/>      "mediaType": "application/gml+xml; version=3.2"<br/>    }<br/>  },<br/>  "outputs": {<br/>    "stringOutput": {<br/>      "transmissionMode": "value"<br/>    },<br/>    "measureOutput": {<br/>      "transmissionMode": "value"<br/>    },<br/>    "dateOutput": {<br/>      "transmissionMode": "value"<br/>    },<br/>    "doubleOutput": {<br/>      "transmissionMode": "value"<br/>    },<br/>    "arrayOutput": {<br/>      "transmissionMode": "value"<br/>    },<br/>    "complexObjectOutput": {<br/>      "transmissionMode": "value"<br/>    },<br/>    "geometryOutput": {<br/>      "transmissionMode": "value"<br/>    },<br/>    "boundingBoxOutput": {<br/>      "transmissionMode": "value"<br/>    },<br/>    "imageOutput": {<br/>      "format": { "mediaType": "application/tiff; application=geotiff" },<br/>      "transmissionMode": "value"<br/>    },<br/>    "featureCollectionOutput": {<br/>      "transmissionMode": "value"<br/>    }<br/>  },<br/>  "response": "document"<br/>}</pre>
</div>
</div>
<div id="sc_execute_response"><h3 class="published-heading">7.11.4.  Response</h3><p id="_fa055cf2-cd9e-ee5e-3844-2b61681b2ca2">The manner in which a server responds to a process execution request is determined by the following parameters:</p>
<ul id="_f4ee46a7-c52c-f545-8ae6-0b7b1d1c4b4f">
<li>
<p id="_fed14c31-6922-f07c-9374-4bbcb4aef322">the <a href="#sc_execution_mode">negotiated execution mode</a> (synchronous or asynchronous),</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_9ccc9fe2-9e9d-5d3f-a53f-6902fbca6487">the <tt>response</tt> parameter (<tt>document</tt> or <tt>raw</tt>),</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_4a3216e9-9603-389e-848a-4aa221ac9601">the <tt>transmissionMode</tt> parameter (<tt>value</tt> or <tt>reference</tt>)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_a3865b1c-da89-d7ef-c7a3-c64216e9f9e8">and the number of outputs requested.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="_ac11e1b7-bd5c-56b7-b8ec-b7d11c8a12a8">The following table maps the possible responses based on the combinations of these execute parameters.</p>
<p class="TableTitle" style="text-align:center;">Table 11 — Table mapping execute responses based on the input parameter values.</p><table class="MsoISOTable" id="table_core_execute_responses"
